subject: On‑prem observability fanout & tracehook runbook (egress fallback options)
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security Team <sec-team@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability for on‑prem Redwood — SIEM fanout question

Hi Rohan,

We're wrapping up the network design for our private deployment of Redwood in our VPC and need guidance on how you recommend exporting logs/traces into our security stack. Two constraints to be aware of:

- Egress is tightly scoped: outbound allowed only to a short list of IPs and ports (443).
- Corporate policy discourages direct cloud object storage egress; we'd prefer direct SIEM ingestion (Splunk/QRadar) but want a fallback if that path is blocked during failover.

Can you outline a recommended fanout pattern (collector sidecar vs central forwarder vs relay) and what you suggest as an operational fallback (batched export, encrypted S3 in a locked account, etc.)? Also need a quick note on how tracehook headers should be preserved when forwarding to our APM.

We'd like to review this with your observability team early next week.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Turner
Head of Platform Engineering — Acme Corp
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability for on‑prem Redwood — SIEM fanout question

Sam — thanks for the clear constraints. High level recommendation below (attachment: egress-fanout-diagram-v1.png and tracehook-sample-headers.txt).

Summary (short):
- Preferred: in‑VPC collector sidecar per node (lightweight Fluent Bit) that performs TLS syslog/HEC -> direct SIEM ingestion to allowed endpoints.
- Fanout: sidecar forwards to a small, fixed set of upstream relay IPs (these are the only egress targets you need to whitelist). Relays do protocol translation if needed (syslog -> HEC).
- Fallback: local encrypted queue + periodic batched transfer to a preapproved S3 bucket over mTLS (only if direct SIEM path fails). The transfer should be time‑boxed and visible in the runbook so it can be audited.

Operational details:
- Networking: allow outbound to 3 relay IPs on 443 and 6514 (TLS syslog). Relays use client certs (mutual TLS) — we can provide certs or you may supply your CA.
- Authentication & rotation: use short‑lived client certs rotated via your KMS (we support automated rotation via the onboarding playbook).
- Message fidelity: preserve tracehook headers (x-redwood-traceid, x-redwood-spanid) at the collector; ensure any translation into HEC includes these headers mapped to HEC fields so the APM links traces to logs. See tracehook-sample-headers.txt for mapping.
- Backpressure/failure: collectors should spool to local encrypted disk in /var/lib/redwood/obsv/spool, with a configurable retention window (default 48h). On sustained egress failure (>15m) the spooling agent will enable batched upload to the fallback S3.

Compliance notes: we default to encrypted-at-rest for spooled data (AES-256) and in-transit via mTLS. If you cannot allow S3 egress at all, we recommend a hammer: provide an on‑prem relay appliance in your DMZ that accepts the fanout and stores the batched files for later pickup by your SIEM team.

Next steps I propose:
1) Security to confirm whitelist process and whether S3 fallback acceptable.
2) Joint run (test evaporation) where we bring up a collector, simulate egress fail, and verify batched upload and trace links.
3) Update your runbook entries and acceptance criteria (we attached an initial runbook template in onprem-obsv-runbook-v1.docx).

I'll be available for a call tomorrow 10:30–11:30 PT to walk through the diagram.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 18 May 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability for on‑prem Redwood — SIEM fanout question

On Wed, May 17, 2028 at 11:03 AM Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the clear constraints. High level recommendation below (attachment: egress-fanout-diagram-v1.png and tracehook-sample-headers.txt).

Quick security checklist and blockers from our side:
- No generic S3 fallback without a signed approval from Acme security. If Acme can provide an approved storage account and KMS policies, encrypted S3 is acceptable.
- All egress must be restricted to explicit IP:port pairs and hostnames; no wildcard domains.
- mTLS required for all forwarder->relay connections. Client certs must be rotated every 30 days and we need a rotation audit log.
- Audit trail: every batched upload must include a signed manifest with SHA256 checksums and a timestamp that maps back to the runbook step ID.
- Retention/purge: confirm retention windows. Redwood default is 45 days for spooled data; if Acme needs longer we need to capture that in the contract.

If Acme cannot approve S3 egress, Rohan's on‑prem relay appliance suggestion is the right path (we will provide a hardened VM image + config). Important: the appliance must run in your DMZ or a zone with outbound edge connectivity to the SIEM.

I'll add these items to the runbook template and include acceptance tests (Jira: OBV-1224).

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Security Lead — Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability for on‑prem Redwood — SIEM fanout question

Thanks all — quick summary and concrete next actions.

Summary of the agreed pattern:
- Primary: per‑node Fluent Bit sidecar -> mTLS -> Redwood relay (3 IPs) -> your SIEMs (protocol translation in relay).
- Fallback: encrypted local spool -> batched upload to preapproved S3 OR pickup by on‑prem relay appliance (if S3 denied).
- Security controls: client cert rotation (30d), spool encryption AES-256, signed manifests for batch uploads, and strict IP whitelisting.
- Tracehooks: preserve x-redwood-traceid/x-redwood-spanid through HEC mapping — Marissa will validate in the integration test.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Acme (Sam): confirm whether S3 fallback is allowed and provide approved storage/KMS details by Tue 2028-05-23.
- Redwood (Marissa + Jonas): prep test harness and runbook changes (deliver by Tue 2028-05-23). Attachments: onprem-obsv-runbook-v1.docx (draft), egress-fanout-diagram-v1.png, tracehook-sample-headers.txt.
- Security (Kimberly): produce rotation/audit checklist and manifest template (deliver by Mon 2028-05-22).

Proposed test window: Wed 2028-05-24 09:00–11:00 PT — run: whitelist test IPs, bring up collector, simulate egress failure, validate spool retention, perform batched upload, and verify trace linking in APM.

If that works for Acme, I'll send a calendar invite and the test checklist.

Cheers,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
